summary: Much stronger than w16 line by line: most objects have concrete, object-true premises with human reactions (the armchair that made grandad miss his own party, the bed the dog brought toast to, the folding screen dropping mid costume change, the kitchen island that retired the dining table, the kneeling chair that straightened a dog, the hat stand that steals hats). The problems are structural. (1) Names are attached to the wrong lines in about 25 objects: Uncommon and Rare names were shuffled (room divider, locker, dog bed, hammock, bench seat, folding chair, picnic table, pet bed, piano bench and others), so Lightblocker sits on the room-splitting line and Flipover on the swaying one. (2) About 30 Legendaries use the template 'Has [done] so many X that it [knows / can tell / could] Y' (coffee table, desk, kitchen counter, nightstand, picnic table, piano bench, footrest, bench seat, mattress topper, pet bed, vanity stool and more), and another dozen use 'for N years / never once / four generations'. (3) Several objects scale one trait over three rarities (coffee table toes, console table keys, cabinet lids, towel rail warmth, pouffe rolling, deckchair that won't open, nesting tables' extra table). (4) Cluster copies: the spinning seats (swivel stool U = hammock chair U, three Epics spinning a toddler), wobbling stools (stool R = step stool R), sleep mask = eye mask, good china (credenza, hutch), pigeonholes (bureau, secretary desk), standing desk = sit-stand desk Epics. Safety: the ladder shelf invites toddlers to climb it, the bean bag Legendary has a teenager jumping off the top bunk, stools wobble while stood on, children spun on stools, the bunk bed's 'two in the gap', the bunk Ultimate 'Lights Out Leap'; the folding screen's 'three shepherds' and the pew's 'Kneelerbench' bring back church content that the tracker says was removed. 'Tall Tipple Tip' is an alcohol word. Moves: about 75 signatures are '<Noun> Startle' (truthful but monotonous), and a handful of Ultimates use rest/sleep/cure words or repeat the Epic name. Replacements are given for every high and medium item.

patterns.pattern: Names sit on the wrong rarity's line (Uncommon/Rare names shuffled, or a name describing another line).
patterns.suggestion: Re-pair names after the lore (write the name for each line, not in a row). Per-field names are given below.

patterns.pattern: Legendary template: 'Has [done] so many X that it [knows / can tell / could / now ...] Y'.
patterns.suggestion: Most are replaced with a feat and a punchline below; a few with a real punchline are left as low notes.

patterns.pattern: Endurance and generations Legendaries: 'for twenty years without', 'for sixty years until', 'four generations', 'every day for five years', 'never once'.
patterns.suggestion: Replaced below (lockers that open the whole corridor, a stool at the top of a mountain, a bureau writing its own complaint letters).

patterns.pattern: One trait scaled across three or four rarities.
patterns.suggestion: Change the line flagged per object.

patterns.pattern: Cluster duplicates: spinning seats (swivel stool U = hammock chair U; swivel stool, stool and hammock chair Epics all spin a toddler); wobbling stools (stool R = step stool R); eye mask = sleep mask (midday dark, sleeping through dawn/festival); good china (credenza U/L, hutch R/L); pigeonholes (bureau C, secretary desk U); standing desk E = sit-stand desk E; the card table and folding chair both 'live behind the door'; coffee table E = footrest E (every shin).
patterns.suggestion: Replacements below keep one owner per premise.

patterns.pattern: Safety: climbing furniture (ladder shelf R), jumping off a top bunk (bean bag L), standing on a wobbling stool (stool R, step stool R), spinning toddlers on stools (stool E, swivel stool E, hammock chair E), overloading a bunk bed (bunk bed L) and 'Lights Out Leap'.
Religious and alcohol leftovers: 'three shepherds' in the school play (nativity), 'Kneelerbench' on the hall-bench pew, 'Tall Tipple Tip', 'Cellar Heat' on the wine rack.
Legendary name shapes: about 60 'The X That Y' plus a cluster of titles (Lord, Lady, Baroness, Countess, Grand Duke, Grand Marshal, Grand Unfolder, Sir, Her Majesty).
patterns.suggestion: New Legendary names below avoid both; keep at most four titles in the batch.

patterns.pattern: Ultimates with rest, sleep, cure or guard words on attacks, or repeating the Epic name (Long Siesta, Cold Feet Cure, Feet Up, Catnap Curl, Quilt Cover, Combination Lock, Coat Mountain, Office Rodeo, Kitchen Carousel Twirl, Steamy Bath).
About 75 signatures are '<Noun> Startle' (stun on Leg Sweep / Lullaby). Truthful, but the batch reads as one move.
patterns.suggestion: Vary with flash, jolt, bump, clatter, creak words.

patterns.pattern: Flat 'waits / sits / stands ... waiting for' Commons with no joke (bench, rocking horse, footrest, hammock, coat rack, pool table, vanity stool, step stool, sawhorse).
patterns.suggestion: Fixed where the line is flagged; aim for a small consequence.
